newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-BATTEN RUNS EIGHTH-FASTEST HURDLES TIME.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BATTEN RUNS EIGHTH-FASTEST HURDLES TIME.

text.p: Kim Batten, promising her women's 400-meter hurdles world record would fall this year, pulled away from Tonja Buford-Bailey down the stretch and ran the eighth fastest time ever, 52.97 seconds, at the U.S. athletics championships on Saturday.

"That world record is definitely going to go down, whether it's me or somebody else," said Batten, who set the record of 52.61 at the 1995 world championships. "I think low 52s or possibly 51 is possible."
Fellow Olympian Jearl Miles-Clark added the year's leading women's 400-meter time of 49.40 seconds as the United States continued to select its world championship team.
Familiar faces Butch Reynolds and Johnny Gray will not be competing in Athens.
World record holder Reynolds ran out of steam in the 400 meters and finished sixth in 44.98 seconds. Gray, the U.S. 800-meter record holder, placed fifth in his final in 1:45.37.
Only the top three finishers in each final qualified for the U.S. team for the August world championship.
Antonio Pettigrew, the 1991 world champion, bested newcomers Tyree Washington and Jerome Young for the men's 400-meter victory in 44.65 seconds.
Mark Everett claimed the men's 800-meter title in one minute, 44.37 seconds.
In qualifying, Bryan Bronson added the year's second-fastest 400-meter hurdles time -- 48.19 seconds -- to his list-leading 48.16 seconds.
The women's 100-meter hurdles also were fast as Melissa Morrison clocked 12.78 seconds and Kim Carson ran 12.88 seconds in first-round action.
New women's 100-meter star Marion Jones became a threat to make the American team in a second event with a leap of 6.69 meters (21 feet, 11 1/2 inches) in the long jump.
That put her third in qualifying for Sunday's final, just ahead of Jackie Joyner-Kersee at 6.67 meters (21 feet, 10 3/4 inches).
